title: How Astronauts Repaired Hubble in Orbit
description: Hubble launched in 1990 with a microscopic mirror flaw that blurred its view of the cosmos. Spacewalking astronauts later installed corrective optics to give the telescope sharp sight.
hook_card: The telescope that was born blind

shots.narration: On April 24, 1990, space shuttle Discovery launched the Hubble Space Telescope into orbit above Earth.
The observatory was equipped with a 2.4-metre mirror designed to capture deep space.
However, the mirror was ground to the wrong shape by about two microns, a fiftieth of a hair's width.
Because of this tiny manufacturing error, the initial images returned from the telescope were blurred.
In December 1993, shuttle astronauts installed corrective optics during five spacewalks, making its vision sharp.
Five servicing missions, the last in 2009, replaced cameras, gyroscopes, and solar panels over time.
Hubble orbits about 540 kilometres above Earth, completing a full circle around the planet every 95 minutes.
Through these astronaut repairs, the space telescope has made more than 1.6 million observations.
